newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on Rao court appearance.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on Rao court appearance.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse closed lower on nervous selling by operators amid political tension following former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's court appearance in a forgery case, brokers said.
The indicative Delhi Stock Exchange index closed 7.50 points down at 731.39.
"The report of Rao's appearance before the special judge brought some kind of nervousness among bull operators and they indulged in panic selling," said Anil Mishra of brokers Jade Investments.
Rao appeared in court on Wednesday to face criminal forgery charges from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police.
On September 26 the CBI charged Rao and the three others with involvement in an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, a Congress party rebel who later became prime minister.
They are alleged to have forged documents which aimed to show that Singh's son held $21 million in a bank account on the Caribbean island of St Kitts.

I.T.C. sharply fell 18.10 rupees or 5.6 percent to 301.20 on following panic selling on the arrest of a director of I.T.C. Ltd and three former company officials on alleged violation of foreign exchange rules in export deals.
Reliance Industries fell 5.25 rupees to 205.25 while ACC lost 22.90 rupees at 1,517.10.
TELCO dropped 15.30 rupees to 412 and Larsen and Toubro lost six rupees at 224.50.
